---
title: "Examples"
---

## Basic Usage

State persists across cells:

````markdown
```{term}
export GREETING="Hello from quarto-term"
```

```{term}
echo $GREETING
```
````

## Multi-Line Commands

Loops and other multi-line constructs work automatically via PS2 detection:

````markdown
```{term}
for i in 1 2 3; do
  echo "Item $i"
done
```
````

## ANSI Colors

Colored output renders faithfully:

````markdown
```{term}
printf '\033[31mred\033[0m \033[32mgreen\033[0m \033[34mblue\033[0m\n'
```
````

## Fullscreen Applications

Capture TUI apps by splitting the interaction across cells:

````markdown
```{term}
nyancat #! enter: false, expect-prompt: false
```

```{term}
#| fullscreen: true
enter #! literal: false, delay: 1.0, hold: 5.0
```

```{term}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
ctrl-c #! literal: false, hold: 0.5
```
````

The first cell types the command without pressing Enter. The second cell presses Enter, waits 1 second, then holds for 5 seconds while capturing the fullscreen output. The third cell sends Ctrl-C to exit (hidden from output).

## Interrupting a Command

Send a long-running command, then interrupt it:

````markdown
```{term}
sleep 100 #! expect-prompt: false
ctrl-c #! literal: false, delay: 0.5, expect-prompt: true
```
````

The `expect-prompt: false` tells quarto-term not to wait for a prompt after `sleep 100` (since it won't return one). After 0.5 seconds, Ctrl-C is sent to interrupt it.

## Arrow Key Navigation

Recall and re-execute the previous command:

````markdown
```{term}
echo "first command"
up #! literal: false, hold: 0.3
enter #! literal: false
```
````

## Human Typing with Recordings

Create a realistic terminal recording:

````markdown
---
title: "Demo"
format: html
engine: markdown
term:
  shell: zsh
  typing:
    mode: human
    speed: 120
    error-rate: 0.02
  record: "demo.cast"
---

```{term}
echo 'This is typed with realistic human timing'
```
````

## Working with Files

````markdown
```{term}
echo "line 1" > /tmp/demo.txt
echo "line 2" >> /tmp/demo.txt
cat /tmp/demo.txt
```
````

## Piping

Multi-line pipes work naturally:

````markdown
```{term}
seq 1 5 |
paste -sd+ |
bc
```
````
